source_licence_note: Official Environment Agency/Defra and Ordnance Survey public documentation; dataset licensing/attribution applies.

official_sources.title: LIDAR Composite Digital Terrain Model (DTM) - 1m
official_sources.finding: The current official 1 m DTM covers about 99% of England, is supplied as 5 km GeoTIFF tiles aligned to the OS National Grid, uses metres and Ordnance Datum Newlyn, EPSG:27700/OSTN15, and states ±15 cm RMSE vertical accuracy for contributing surveys.
official_sources.limitation: This is product-level metadata; it does not provide the target parcel cells or measured parcel extrema.

official_sources.title: Defra Data Services Platform 1 m Composite DTM
official_sources.finding: The EA service confirms 1 m DTM coverage, source-survey period, newest/best-resolution merge policy, bilinear resampling where needed, vertical accuracy ±15 cm RMSE, EPSG:27700, and provides survey-data, metadata-index, WMS/WCS/WMTS and feature-service access routes.
official_sources.limitation: The composite may contain surveys from different dates; target-cell provenance must be read from the metadata index.

official_sources.title: LIDAR DTM Time Stamped Tiles
official_sources.finding: The time-stamped DTM archive contains site-specific terrain rasters at 25 cm, 50 cm, 1 m and 2 m resolution, supplied as 5 km GeoTIFF zipfiles aligned to the OS Grid, with heights in metres referenced to Ordnance Datum Newlyn and stated ±15 cm RMSE vertical accuracy.
official_sources.limitation: Survey-specific geoid/transformation provenance varies by survey date and must be checked in metadata.

official_sources.title: LIDAR DSM Time Stamped Tiles
official_sources.finding: The time-stamped DSM archive includes buildings, vegetation and other surface objects; it is distinct from bare-earth DTM and reports the same metre/ODN/OS-grid framework and ±15 cm RMSE product specification.
official_sources.limitation: DSM must not be substituted for terrain height difference when the required semantic is bare-earth topography.

official_sources.title: Survey Data Catalogue projection information
official_sources.finding: EA states survey data are supplied in OSGB36 British National Grid with elevations above Ordnance Datum Newlyn; the LiDAR Composite uses the OSTN15 geoid model, while time-stamped and point-cloud surveys require survey metadata to identify the geoid model, with OSGM15 used for surveys after 26 August 2016.
official_sources.limitation: Older surveys can use earlier geoid models, so cross-survey height comparison must not assume one transformation epoch/model.

official_sources.title: Survey Data Catalogue vertical accuracy of LiDAR
official_sources.finding: EA specifies absolute height error less than ±15 cm RMSE against Ground Truth Survey and expects relative/random height error no more than ±5 cm.
official_sources.limitation: Absolute RMSE and relative/random error are different quantities and must not be arithmetically collapsed into one undocumented accuracy number.

official_sources.title: OSGM15 national geoid model
official_sources.finding: OSGM15 converts ETRS89 ellipsoid height to orthometric height; on mainland Britain it directly provides ODN heights. OS states nominal geoid-model accuracy of 8 mm rms on mainland UK and recommends OSGM15 with OS Net for high-accuracy orthometric heighting.
official_sources.limitation: The 8 mm model figure is not the same as LiDAR survey RMSE and must remain a separate uncertainty component.

official_sources.title: OSTN15 national grid transformation
official_sources.finding: OSTN15 is the definitive OSGB36/ETRS89 grid transformation and uses a 1 km transformation grid with bilinear interpolation; OS says a simple Helmert transformation is only suitable at about metre-level accuracy and OSTN15 is required for precise National Grid work.
official_sources.limitation: Horizontal transformation correctness alone does not prove vertical datum or target raster-cell identity.

official_sources.title: OS datum, ellipsoid and EPSG information
official_sources.finding: OS documents EPSG identifiers including OSGB36 National Grid 27700, ODN vertical datum 7405, OSTN15 7953/7709 and OSGM15 ODN transformation 7711, enabling explicit CRS and vertical-operation ledger checks.
official_sources.limitation: Identifiers must be matched to the actual source and transformation pipeline rather than merely recorded.

official_sources.title: Approximate WGS84 to OSGB36/ODN transformation warning
official_sources.finding: OS warns the approximate Helmert transformation can have errors up to 3.5 m at 95% confidence horizontally and vertically and must not be used where better accuracy is required.
official_sources.limitation: This source is a rejection guard, not a preferred high-accuracy transformation method.

official_sources.title: Ordnance Datum Newlyn
official_sources.finding: OS describes ODN as the mainland Britain orthometric/mean-sea-level height datum and warns that legacy bench marks may have movement/subsidence risk; modern precise height control is accessed through GNSS/OS Net with OSGM15.
official_sources.limitation: Bench-mark network statements do not validate any target parcel raster value.

official_sources.title: EA time-stamped survey supporting adjustment grid
official_sources.finding: EA publishes coverage metadata and an OSGM02-to-OSGM15 Adjustment Grid alongside time-stamped LiDAR datasets, supporting explicit normalization/provenance checks when older surveys and OSGM15-era data are compared.
official_sources.limitation: An adjustment resource being available does not prove that a target asset needs or has received that adjustment.
